title: min_cost_matching docstring promises a second optimization pass that never runs
description:
The min_cost_matching docstring (src/circle_squaring/matching.py:122-127) ends: 'the radius escalates until a perfect matching exists, then one more optimization pass runs at that radius.'

No such pass exists. The loop at matching.py:133 builds the sparse cost graph for radius r, calls min_weight_full_bipartite_matching, and on success returns immediately at matching.py:156. A ValueError (no perfect matching at that radius) continues to the next r. There is exactly one solve per radius and the function exits on the first that succeeds.

The result is not wrong — LAPJVsp already returns the minimum-cost perfect matching for the graph it was given, so a second pass at the same radius would be a no-op. The defect is that the docstring describes an algorithm the code does not implement, which invites a maintainer to either 'restore' a redundant pass or to assume a refinement step is protecting solution quality when nothing is.

Found by a model-review sweep and verified against source by hand.
acceptance_criteria: The docstring describes the actual control flow: escalate the radius until a perfect matching exists, solve once at that radius, return.
